case.headline: A filed report explains this 35.4 ppb episode.

reasoning.claim: The monitor recorded 35.4 ppb at its peak on Feb 13, 2023, 11:00 PM, against a background near 0.5 ppb, over 6 hours.
Through the episode the wind came from the south-south-east, modelled.
The closest filed report is incident 395434 from Port Arthur Refinery, listing 449.04 pounds, with 100% of the episode's hours inside its window.

innocent_explanations: A release below the reportable quantity would leave no filed report at all.
Permitted, routine emissions can build up when the air is still and the plume stays low.
what_would_settle_it: Sub-hourly data from the monitor for this window, which would show whether the rise was a sharp plume or a slow build.
Any complaint or investigation records the agency holds for this date.
case.request_draft:
To: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, Public Information Coordinator
Subject: Public information request, air monitoring and incident records, Port Arthur and Beaumont

Dear Public Information Coordinator,

Under the Texas Public Information Act, I request copies of the following records.

1. All ambient air monitoring data, at the finest time resolution held, for monitor 48-245-0011 from Feb 13, 2023, 11:00 PM to Feb 14, 2023, 5:00 AM local time.
2. Any citizen complaints, investigation reports or field notes relating to air quality in Port Arthur and Beaumont for that period.
3. Any emission event, maintenance, startup or shutdown notifications received for facilities in Jefferson or Orange County covering that period, including any submitted after the deadline.

This is a request for public records. It is not an allegation that any facility did anything improper.

If any portion is withheld, please cite the exemption claimed and release the remainder. If fees will exceed $50, please contact me first with an estimate.

Sincerely,
[your name]
[your address]
[your email and phone]
